Prerequisite: The FortiWeb registered with Fortinet Customer Service & Support, with each purchased service contract registered to its serial number
What it enables: Firmware updates, FortiGuard services, and FortiSandbox services, which require product registration; the service contracts P3 to P11 apply only to a registered unit
How to put it in place: Register the serial number at the Fortinet Customer Service & Support website (Register/Renew) and enter each contract registration code; check the Support Contract row in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Registering your FortiWeb" (firmware updates, FortiGuard services, and FortiSandbox services require product registration), "Appendix F: How to purchase and renew FortiGuard licenses", and "Licenses" (Support Contract)

Prerequisite: A path from the FortiWeb to the FortiGuard Distribution Network (FDN): DNS, routes, and firewall rules to the Internet, an explicit web proxy, another FortiWeb acting as an FDS proxy, or, for FortiWeb-VM license validation in a closed network, a FortiManager with its built-in FDS
What it enables: Validation of the FortiGuard licenses, and downloads of current signatures, IP lists, credential databases, and engine packages
How to put it in place: Test the connection with Update Now in GUI: System > Config > FortiGuard (Override default FortiGuard address for an FDS proxy); for FortiManager, config system autoupdate override; set status enable; set address <FORTIMANAGER_IP_AND_PORT>; set fail-over disable; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Connecting to FortiGuard services" (without connecting to FortiGuard, FortiWeb cannot detect the latest threats), "License validation with FortiManager", and "Accessing FortiGuard via a proxy"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard FortiWeb Security Service contract
What it enables: Updates of the attack signatures, predefined data types, predefined suspicious URLs, global allow list objects, Fuzzy Web Shell DB, and Known Bots DB (the signatures for malicious robots)
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, alone or in a bundle, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (FortiGuard services: FortiWeb Security Service), "Blocklisting known bots" (predefined bot signatures are kept up to date with a FortiGuard Security Service subscription), and "Appendix F: How to purchase and renew FortiGuard licenses"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Antivirus Service contract
What it enables: Virus signature updates for antivirus scanning of uploaded files (regular and extended virus databases)
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (FortiGuard services: FortiWeb Antivirus Service) and "Choosing the virus signature database & decompression buffer"

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard IP Reputation (IRIS) Service contract
What it enables: Updates of the known botnets, malicious clients, and anonymizing proxies that IP reputation blocks
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (FortiGuard services: FortiWeb IP Reputation Service) and "IP Reputation - Blocklisting source IPs with poor reputation" (IP reputation knowledge is updated with a subscription and a connection to the service)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Credential Stuffing Defense Service contract
What it enables: The Credential Stuffing Defense database, which FortiWeb does not have built in (at least one FortiGuard update installs it), and its online check
How to put it in place: Purchase the service, register it (P1), and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (FortiGuard services: FortiWeb Credential Stuffing Defense Service) and "User Tracking" (Credential Stuffing Defense: no built-in database; at least one FortiGuard update is required)

Prerequisite: A Geo DB contract
What it enables: Updates of the Geo IP database that Geo IP policies use to match countries and regions
How to put it in place: Register the contract (P1) and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Licenses" (Additional services: Geo DB)

Prerequisite: A FortiGuard Data Loss Prevention service license, alone or bundled with Advanced Bot Protection
What it enables: The FortiGuard DLP dictionaries of predefined data patterns; without the service only the basic DLP settings are available
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the license (P1), update the FortiGuard DLP database, and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "FortiGuard DLP service license" and "Licenses" (Additional services: Data Loss Prevention (DLP))

Prerequisite: A FortiAppSec Cloud Advanced Bot Protection license, registered on the Support site with the same account email address as the FortiWeb, validated by logging in to FortiAppSec Cloud, and a connection from the FortiWeb to that cloud service (a service outside the enclave, used only if authorized)
What it enables: Advanced Bot Protection policies and the login status reporting to the service
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the license (P1), log in to FortiAppSec Cloud, then select Enable Advanced Bot Protection in GUI: Dashboard > Status (System Information widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Configuring Advanced Bot Protection policy" (enabling the ABP service in FortiWeb) and "Licenses" (Advanced Bot Protection)

Prerequisite: A Client-Side Protection service license (a 30-day trial license is available for evaluation)
What it enables: Client-side protection policies; without a license the module cannot be configured in the GUI or the CLI
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the license (P1), and check its status in GUI: Dashboard > Status (Licenses widget)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Client-Side Protection (8.0.0)" (a valid license for the Client-Side Protection service is required) and "Licenses" (Client-Side Protection)

Prerequisite: A FortiSandbox appliance or FortiSandbox-VM reachable from the FortiWeb, or, for FortiWeb Cloud Sandbox, a FortiWeb FortiGuard Sandbox Cloud Service subscription on a registered FortiWeb (a cloud service outside the enclave, used only if authorized)
What it enables: Submission of uploaded files to a sandbox, and the sandbox malware signature database
How to put it in place: An organization FortiSandbox, then config system fortisandbox; set type fsa; set server <FORTISANDBOX_IP>; end; for the cloud service, purchase and register the subscription (P1)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system fortisandbox (the FortiWeb Cloud Sandbox option requires a registered FortiWeb and a FortiWeb FortiGuard Sandbox Cloud Service subscription); FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "To configure a FortiSandbox connection" and "Licenses" (FortiSandbox Cloud)

Prerequisite: A server policy for the protected application: a virtual server, a server pool with the back-end web servers, and the web protection profile, enabled
What it enables: Every WAF setting made in a web protection profile, a server policy, a server pool, or an object they use; until a server policy applies them they inspect no traffic
How to put it in place: config server-policy policy; edit <POLICY>; set vserver <VSERVER>; set server-pool <POOL>; set web-protection-profile <PROFILE>; set status enable; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Configuring an HTTP server policy"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, server-policy policy; Chapter 16 row *Server policies, virtual servers, and server pools*

Prerequisite: The DoD PKI on the FortiWeb: the DoD root and intermediate CA certificates imported where the setting selects them, a reachable CRL distribution point or OCSP responder, a DoD CA that signs the FortiWeb's certificate requests, and certificates issued by that PKI to the administrators and users who present them
What it enables: Certificate (PKI) administrator login, client certificate verification with CRL and OCSP checks, verification of back-end server certificates, and validation of the LDAPS, OAuth, FortiClient EMS, FortiGate, and IP address connector servers
How to put it in place: config system certificate ca; edit <DOD_CA>; set certificate <CA_CERTIFICATE_PEM>; next; end and config system certificate crl; edit <DOD_CRL>; set type HTTP; set url <CRL_URL>; next; end; administrator CA certificates in GUI: System > Admin > Certificates (Admin Cert CA)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system certificate ca, system certificate crl, system certificate ocsp-responder, and system admin-certificate ca (CA certificates are required to create a PKI user); FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "How to apply PKI client authentication (personal certificates)" and "Revoking certificates"

Prerequisite: Certificates with private keys issued to the FortiWeb by the DoD PKI (from a certificate signing request made on the FortiWeb, or held in a network HSM, P15): one for the web UI, one for each HTTPS service, and a client certificate where the FortiWeb authenticates to a server
What it enables: HTTPS management with a trusted certificate, HTTPS offloading and its TLS settings, HTTP to HTTPS redirection and HSTS, syslog over TLS with a client certificate, and a custom SAML service provider certificate
How to put it in place: Generate a CSR or import the certificate in GUI: Server Objects > Certificates > Local (services) or GUI: System > Admin > Certificates (web UI and syslog client certificate)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Generating a certificate signing request" and "Uploading a server certificate"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system certificate local and system admin-certificate local

Prerequisite: A network HSM that FortiWeb supports, reachable from the FortiWeb: a Thales Luna Network HSM 5, 6, or 7 (SafeNet), or a Securosys Primus HSM, with a partition assigned to the FortiWeb as a registered client
What it enables: Private keys kept in the HSM for HTTPS offloading and, with Primus, for the web UI certificate
How to put it in place: An organization HSM, then config server-policy setting; set hsm enable; set hsm-manufacturer <HSM_MANUFACTURER>; end, and the partition in GUI: System > Config > Luna HSM (or the Securosys Primus HSM page)
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Using Luna HSM" ("System compatibility and upgrade requirements": Luna Network HSM 5, 6, and 7; older appliance models are not supported) and "Support Using Primus HSM Certificates for Admin GUI Access (8.0.0)"

Prerequisite: A FortiWeb hardware appliance that supports TPM, or a FortiWeb-VM on a hypervisor that provides a virtual TPM (vTPM)
What it enables: The TPM-based device-specific key that encrypts configuration passwords and certificates, and the stronger method of configuration file encryption, which uses that key
How to put it in place: Deploy a supported appliance, or enable vTPM for the virtual machine; then config system encryption-method; set private-encryption-key enable; end
Source: FortiWeb 7.6.10 Administration Guide, "Enhanced private data protection with TPM encryption (7.6.3)" (Platform Support: hardware TPM on supported appliances, vTPM for FortiWeb-VM); FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system encryption-method and system global (encrypt-cfgfile)

Prerequisite: A FortiWeb platform that supports FIPS-CC mode: a hardware appliance, or a FortiWeb-VM image that the CLI Reference does not list as unsupported (it lists the Hyper-V, KVM, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, and Alibaba Cloud images, the pay-as-you-go images, and the FortiWeb cloud images); the fips-ciphers mode is supported only on FortiWeb-VM in AWS and Azure
What it enables: FIPS-CC mode and the ciphers it allows
How to put it in place: Choose the platform and image before deployment, checking the image name against the list in the CLI Reference
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system fips-cc (the images that do not support FIPS-CC mode, and the images that support fips-ciphers mode)

Prerequisite: A FortiWeb hardware model with a fail-to-wire (bypass) port pair, in standalone mode (not HA) and in True Transparent Proxy, Transparent Inspection, or WCCP mode, with the traffic on that port pair
What it enables: The fail-open bypass ports
How to put it in place: Choose a model and port pair that the Administration Guide lists, then set the behavior in GUI: Network > Fail-open
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Fail-to-wire for power loss/reboots" (supported operation modes, standalone only, and the port pairs of each model); FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system fail-open (the setting name varies by model)

Prerequisite: The other members of the HA group: identical FortiWeb appliances with the same firmware (for FortiWeb-VM, valid non-trial licenses and the same ports, memory, and vCPUs), at least one heartbeat port link between the members, a redundant network topology, and, if the group uses FortiGuard services, licenses and registration for every member
What it enables: HA clusters and their failover, heartbeat, health check synchronization, and manual failover
How to put it in place: Cable the heartbeat link and the redundant topology, license and register every member, then on each unit config system ha; set mode active-passive; set group-id <GROUP_ID>; set priority <PRIORITY>; set hbdev <HEARTBEAT_PORT>; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "HA requirements" and "Basic settings" (step 1: license and register all members when the group uses FortiGuard services; FortiWeb-VM HA cannot use trial licenses)

Prerequisite: A reachable organization LDAP (over LDAPS), RADIUS, or TACACS+ server with the administrator accounts, and a remote administrator group that names its query
What it enables: Remote administrator accounts, including wildcard accounts, so that the authentication server enforces the account and password rules
How to put it in place: An organization authentication service, then config user radius-user; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_SERVER>; set secret <SECRET>; next; end and config user admin-usergrp; edit <GROUP>; config members; edit 1; set type radius; set radius-name <RADIUS>; next; end; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, user ldap-user, user radius-user, user tacacs+-user, and user admin-usergrp; Chapter 16 row *Remote administrator authentication (RADIUS, LDAP, TACACS+) through administrator groups*

Prerequisite: An organization SAML identity provider with the FortiWeb registered as a service provider
What it enables: Administrator single sign-on with SAML
How to put it in place: An organization SAML IdP; the FortiWeb SAML settings name its entity ID and single sign-on and logout URLs
Source: FortiWeb 7.6.10 Administration Guide, "Admin user Single Sign-On with SAML (7.6.0)"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system saml and system sso-admin

Prerequisite: An administrator access profile that grants the administrator's role
What it enables: Local and single sign-on administrator accounts with the access of their role
How to put it in place: config system accprofile; edit <PROFILE>; set admingrp r; set sysgrp r; set loggrp r; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system accprofile; Chapter 16 row *Access profiles (none, read, write, or read-write per permission group)*

Prerequisite: Another local administrator account with the prof_admin access profile
What it enables: Disabling the default admin account, which requires at least one other fully privileged local administrator
How to put it in place: config system admin; edit <ADMIN>; set type local-user; set access-profile prof_admin; set password <PASSWORD_15_CHARS_MIN>; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system global (default-admin: disabling the default admin account requires another local administrator with the prof_admin access profile)

Prerequisite: Administrative domains enabled and defined, with the protected servers assigned to them
What it enables: Restricting administrators to the ADOMs they manage
How to put it in place: Back up the configuration, then as admin config system global; set adom-admin enable; end, and define the ADOMs
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, "Administrative domains (ADOMs)" (To enable ADOMs) and system global (adom-admin); FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Administrative domains (ADOMs)"

Prerequisite: Organization authentication servers for the users of Site Publish, reachable from the FortiWeb: an LDAP, RADIUS (or RADSEC), or Kerberos server, a SAML identity provider, or an OAuth or OIDC authorization server, with the user accounts
What it enables: Site Publish authentication, single sign-on, and authorization of users, and the related password change, token, and SAML features
How to put it in place: An organization authentication service, then its server entry, for example config user ldap-user; edit <LDAP>; set server <LDAP_SERVER>; set ssl-connection enable; set protocol ldaps; set ca-cert <CA_CERT>; next; end, in the authentication server pool of the Site Publish rule
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Site Publishing (Single sign-on)", "Adding servers to an authentication server pool", "Configuring a Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) server pool", "Using Kerberos authentication delegation", and "OAuth authorization & OIDC authentication"

Prerequisite: A FortiAuthenticator as the RADIUS server, with FortiToken for two-factor authentication
What it enables: FortiAuthenticator authorization and FortiToken Mobile push notification for Site Publish users
How to put it in place: An organization FortiAuthenticator; the RADIUS server entry names it
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Two-factor authentication" (FortiToken Cloud tokens with FortiAuthenticator as the RADIUS server; enable fac-push); FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, user radius-user (fac-push)

Prerequisite: A FortiClient EMS server reachable from the FortiWeb over HTTPS, with the endpoints it manages
What it enables: Zero Trust Network Access: EMS tags and client certificates for ZTNA rules, and the EMS connector
How to put it in place: An organization FortiClient EMS; the EMS connector names it
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA)"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system endpoint-control fctems

Prerequisite: A FortiGate that the FortiWeb can reach on the FortiGate's administrative access port, with an account for the FortiWeb
What it enables: Fetch URL and Quarantine IP: blocking the IP addresses that the FortiGate quarantines
How to put it in place: config system fortigate-integration; set server <FORTIGATE_IP>; set protocol HTTPS; set port 443; set username <USERNAME>; set password <PASSWORD>; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system fortigate-integration (the FortiGate address and port used for administrative access, and the user name and password)

Prerequisite: A web server (HTTP or HTTPS) that publishes an external IP address list, or a STIX/TAXII server, reachable from the FortiWeb
What it enables: The IP address connector and the policies that use its addresses
How to put it in place: An organization IP list source; the IP address connector names it
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "IP Address Connector"; FortiWeb 7.6.10 Administration Guide, "STIX/TAXII Support for IP Address Connector (7.6.4)"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system external-resource

Prerequisite: An ICAP server reachable from the FortiWeb
What it enables: ICAP scanning of uploaded files
How to put it in place: An organization ICAP server, then config system icapserver; set server <ICAP_SERVER>; set ssl enable; set port 11344; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system icapserver; FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "ICAP Server"

Prerequisite: A central syslog server or SIEM that accepts syslog over TLS (with an IPv6 address for IPv6 syslog)
What it enables: Off-loading the event and attack logs, in JSON or CEF where needed
How to put it in place: An organization syslog server; the syslog policy names it
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Configuring Syslog settings"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, log syslog-policy; Chapter 16 row *Remote syslog servers (syslog policies, TLS)*

Prerequisite: An on-premises FortiAnalyzer that accepts the FortiWeb as a log source, and a FortiAnalyzer policy that names it
What it enables: Logging to FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: An organization FortiAnalyzer, then config log fortianalyzer-policy; edit <FAZ_POLICY>; config fortianalyzer-server-list; edit 1; set ip-address <FAZ_IP>; next; end; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Configuring FortiAnalyzer policies"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, log fortianalyzer-policy

Prerequisite: A reachable SMTP server (with STARTTLS and an account if it requires authentication), and an email policy with the recipients
What it enables: Alert email to the ISSO and administrators
How to put it in place: An organization mail server, then config log email-policy; edit <EMAIL_POLICY>; set mailto1 <ISSO_EMAIL>; set smtp-server <SMTP_SERVER>; set connection-security STARTTLS; set smtp-auth enable; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Alert email"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, log email-policy

Prerequisite: Internal NTP servers reachable over a protected path, with their authentication keys for NTP authentication (7.6.1 or later)
What it enables: Synchronized, authenticated system time
How to put it in place: Organization NTP servers; the NTP settings name them and their keys
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system ntp; FortiWeb 7.6.10 Administration Guide, "Enhanced system time reliability (7.6.1)"

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager configured with the same user and security settings and loaded with the Fortinet MIBs, and SNMP access on the FortiWeb interface it connects through
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and traps
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, then config system interface; edit <MGMT_PORT>; set allowaccess HTTPS ssh snmp; next; end
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "SNMP traps & queries" (SNMP access must be enabled on the network interface through which the SNMP manager connects)

Prerequisite: File servers reachable from the FortiWeb: an SFTP server and account for configuration backups and restores, and a TFTP or FTP server for firmware images downloaded, with their checksums, from the Fortinet support site
What it enables: Scheduled encrypted backups to another system, configuration and certificate restore, and firmware upgrades from the CLI
How to put it in place: Organization file servers; the backup, restore, and upgrade commands name them
Source: FortiWeb 8.0.8 Administration Guide, "Backups" and "Upgrading the firmware"; FortiWeb 8.0.8 CLI Reference, system backup and execute restore
